metadata.description: A GTM operating system in Notion, built by plugins rather than by a consultant. Six databases, created once, written to by six plugins that never call each other.

plugins.name: setup
plugins.description: Creates the six Notion databases every other gtm-operator plugin reads and writes, wires the relations between them, and writes the one config file they all share. Explains the model before it asks anything, and asks five questions rather than twelve.

plugins.name: calendar
plugins.description: The GTM calendar: what is happening in market, and when. Shows what else is already aimed at the same people before it writes anything, asks how it went when a row is marked done, and answers what an audience is receiving for a window. Needs the setup plugin, which it reads config from and never calls.

plugins.name: process
plugins.description: The Process library: the living reference of how and why things are done. Writes one artifact from free-form notes in the body template its type calls for, after checking whether the library already has it. Finds the artifact that answers a question and says whether it is still worth trusting. Changes an artifact that already exists, and says what has gone stale or was never verified. Fills the library from documents, conversations and call transcripts you already have, one approval at a time. Needs the setup plugin, which it reads config from and never calls.

plugins.name: memos
plugins.description: Time-stamped communication, append-only. Writes one memo of any of seven types from free-form notes, turns a meeting into a record of what it decided, assembles the recurring team update from Projects, Calendar, Memos and Tasks rather than from memory, and finds what was said about something and when, following corrections to the end of the chain. There is no update skill and there never will be: a correction is a new memo. Needs the setup plugin, which it reads config from and never calls.
